result_semantic_payload.summary: Both USDT transfers visible in this device's logs were performed under the account "chenwei" in /logs/app1.log — the only log containing TRANSFER events: 30,000 USDT at 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12,000 USDT at 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both sent to destination TBait8888Wallet, each inside a successful LOGIN session sourced from external IPs 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 respectively. The same-named "chenwei" account in /logs/app2.log CANNOT be treated as the same person: /README.txt states the two systems are unrelated and share no account database, the two logs show disjoint source-IP ranges (external 203.0.113.77/198.51.100.23 vs internal 10.20.0.5/10.20.0.9), and no shared identifier (SID, employee ID, device binding) exists in the evidence. Attribution to the physical employee "chenwei (finance dept, office workstation)" is likewise not established: the transfer sessions originated from external IPs rather than the described office workstation, and the logs record only the account name, not the operating person. Account "liuyu" appears only with a LOGIN and a DOWNLOAD in app1.log and performed no transfers.

claim_candidates.text: The USDT transfers visible in the logs were performed by the account 'chenwei' in /logs/app1.log: 30,000 USDT to TBait8888Wallet at 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12,000 USDT to TBait8888Wallet at 2024-03-02 22:43:55. app1.log is the only log containing TRANSFER events.

Both chenwei TRANSFER events in app1.log occurred within authenticated sessions (LOGIN result=success) originating from external, non-RFC1918 IP addresses: 203.0.113.77 (2024-03-01 09:14:22, preceding the 30,000 USDT transfer) and 198.51.100.23 (2024-03-02 22:41:10, preceding the 12,000 USDT transfer).

The 'chenwei' account in /logs/app2.log performed no transfers; its recorded activity is internal-IP office work: LOGIN from 10.20.0.5 with UPLOAD of /shared/annual-plan.docx (2024-02-20), LOGIN from 10.20.0.9 (2024-02-21), and a PRINT job to printer HQ-3F (2024-02-22).

The same-named 'chenwei' accounts across app1.log and app2.log cannot be treated as the same person on this evidence: /README.txt states the two systems are unrelated and share no account database, and no shared identifier links the accounts.

Attribution of the USDT transfers to the physical employee 'chenwei (finance dept, office workstation)' described in README.txt is NOT supported: the transfer sessions came from external IPs rather than the office workstation, and the logs record only the account name, not the person operating the session.
Account 'liuyu' performed no USDT transfers; its only app1.log activity is a successful LOGIN from 203.0.113.77 at 2024-03-05 11:02:31 and a DOWNLOAD of /reports/q1-analysis.pdf at 11:04:19.

limitations: Evidence is limited to three plain-text log files; no OS-level artifacts (event logs, registry, prefetch, amcache, SRUM) exist to corroborate account usage or execution.
No account database, SID, employee identifier, or device binding is available, so account-to-person mapping across or within the systems cannot be established from this evidence alone.

The logs record account names only; the physical operator of each session cannot be determined. Notably, the transfer sessions originated from external IPs, not the 'office workstation' described for employee chenwei in README.txt.

Source IPs 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 fall in TEST-NET-3 (RFC 5737 documentation ranges); they are treated here as external (non-internal) addresses as recorded, but their literal values may be sanitized/placeholder data.
warnings: Do not merge the two 'chenwei' accounts into one identity: README.txt explicitly states the systems are unrelated and share no account database.
The USDT transfers are attributed to the chenwei ACCOUNT in app1.log, not proven to be the finance-dept employee; transfer sessions came from external IPs.
